To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Aldosterone receptor antagonists are effective in reducing mortality and morbidity in patients with heart failure.

the aldosterone receptor antagonists eplerenone and spironolactone are associated with a significant reduction in the risk of cardiovascular events and death in patients with heart failure, acute myocardial infarction, and chronic kidney disease.

The cardiovascular benefits of aldosterone receptor antagonists (ARAs) are not limited to patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but extend to all patients with HFrEF or hypertension with diabetes, regardless of ejection fraction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the renin angiotensin system on the cardiovascular system and the development of novel drugs for treating heart failure and hypertension.
the role of potassium in the cardiovascular system, particularly as it relates to the renin-aldosterone system and hypertension.

the development of a new generation of aldosterone receptor antagonists (ARAs) that have a greater affinity and specificity for the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) than for the glucocorticoid receptor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aldosterone is a hormone that maintains sodium homeostasis and potassium balance.
aldosterone is a mineralocorticoid that is primarily responsible for sodium homeostasis and potassium balance.

the major mechanism of action of aldosterone is to promote sodium retention and potassium loss, which is the basis of the current use of aldosterone receptor antagonists (ARA) as adjunctive therapy in the management of heart failure (HF).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that aldosterone is a mineralocorticoid hormone that has a primary role in the maintenance of sodium homeostasis, and a secondary role in the regulation of potassium homeostasis and in the regulation of blood pressure.2,3 The RAS is a complex system that regulates blood pressure and fluid volume through the actions of angiotensins I and II and the renin- angiotensin converting enzyme.

the RAS, and angiotensin in particular, has a major impact on the development and progression of hypertension and cardiovascular disease, including heart failure, and is a major contributor to the development of atherosclerosis.2,3 The major effect of aldosterone is on sodium and potassium balance.

the primary action of aldosterone is on epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) in the distal nephron to increase sodium transport out of the tubular luma.2 The primary action of angiotensins on aldosterone secretion is via the angiotensin type 1 receptor (AT1R) on the zona glomerulosa cells of the adrenal.3 The primary effect of potassium on aldosterone secretion occurs through the potassium channel in the zona glomerulos cell membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aldosterone is an independent risk factor for cardiovascular (CV) disease, and aldosterone antagonists have a favorable CV risk profile.
potassium is not a major determinant of aldosterone secretion in the setting of heart failure.
potassium is an important factor in determining the cardiovascular effects of aldosterone antagonists, particularly spironolactone and eplerenone.
